statement: You receive a non-negative integer n. Print how many bits of n are set. Count with the erase identity - replace n by n AND n-1 until it reaches zero and count the turns - so that the loop runs once per set bit rather than once per bit position.
constraints: The input is a single integer on one line.

example.why: 13 is 1101; three erase steps take it to 1100, then 1000, then 0.

hint: Each erase removes exactly the lowest set bit; the loop guard is simply n different from zero.
mistake: Halving n and testing the remainder each turn - it works, but it runs thirty times on every input instead of once per one.
